text: Ha Tinh secures more than $9.8 bln in investment in 10 months
In the first ten months of 2026, central Ha Tinh province attracted 65 domestic and foreign investment projects, with total registered capital exceeding VND254 trillion (approximately $9.86 billion).

According to data from the Provincial Department of Finance, from the beginning of the year to October 28, 2026, the locality approved investment policies for 59 domestic projects with total registered capital of more than VND241.1 trillion (nearly $9.4 billion), along with six foreign-invested projects worth a combined $505.6 million.

Notably, investment flows have been concentrated in sectors capable of generating long-term growth momentum, particularly manufacturing and processing industries, steel production, energy, and industrial infrastructure development.

Among the most prominent projects are the VinMetal Ha Tinh Steel Manufacturing Plant, with a total investment of over VND79.98 trillion ($3.1 billion); the Vung Ang 3 LNG Power Plant, valued at VND51.43 trillion ($2 billion); and the Thien Cam Eco-Tourism Urban Area, with total investment capital of VND17.211 trillion (nearly $670 million).

Ha Tinh has also attracted several other major projects, including a stainless steel manufacturing plant with investment capital of VND9.8 trillion, the Ky Ninh Wind Power Plant with total investment of VND8.188 trillion, and the Hung Long Industrial Park Infrastructure Development and Business Project, valued at more than VND3.019 trillion.
Alongside capital inflows from major investors, Ha Tinh's private sector has also shown positive momentum.

According to the provincial Department of Finance, from the beginning of the year to October 20, 2026, the province recorded 2,231 newly established enterprises with total registered capital exceeding VND20.689 trillion, representing a nearly 1.6-fold increase in the number of businesses and a 2.3-fold increase in registered capital compared with the same period in 2025.
In addition, 456 enterprises resumed operations, up 17.8% year-on-year.
However, the number of companies completing dissolution procedures also reached 841, nearly 2.8 times higher than in the corresponding period last year.
